rows.acceptance: Authors, works, editions, and files retain separate identities with referential integrity and namespaced provider IDs.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 resolves and records all four source surfaces; ambiguous joins are held rather than collapsed.

rows.acceptance: EPUB, AZW3, and MOBI files are inventoried and EPUB is the preferred initial eBook format.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 maps the existing eBook profile and files without conversion or silent format upgrades.

rows.acceptance: The audiobook target is independent from eBook monitoring and imports the captured M4B file without conflating media kinds.
rows.migration_consequence: B7 adds the independent target/profile and adopts the present audiobook instance; B6 eBook cutover does not create an audiobook target.

rows.acceptance: Existing torrent and Usenet adapters remain the only credential-owning transport boundary for books.
rows.migration_consequence: B4/B5 reuse clients through book-specific intents; B6 imports no connector secret.

rows.acceptance: Book release search uses the existing indexer adapter with explicit book categories and persisted decision evidence.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 preserves source history only; it does not copy indexer URLs or credentials.

rows.acceptance: A completed download is validated and durably published before source cleanup, with retry-safe lifecycle state.
rows.migration_consequence: Books extend the existing guarded lifecycle rather than importing transient queue state.

rows.acceptance: Hardlink is preferred when safe and copy is the explicit fallback; failures leave no partial final asset.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 adopts already-correct files in place and records, but does not rewrite, source paths.

rows.acceptance: Existing filenames are preserved by default because automatic Bookshelf renaming is disabled.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 performs no adoption rename; a future naming policy requires a separate operator opt-in.

rows.acceptance: Published eBooks land under the role-based books root and are visible to Booklore without database mutation.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 verifies existing files under the books root and keeps consumer state external.

rows.acceptance: Published audiobooks land under the role-based audiobooks root and a scan failure is reported without rolling back a durable import.
rows.migration_consequence: B7 verifies/adopts the audiobook file and implements the retryable post-commit Audiobookshelf scan; B6 does not publish audio.

rows.acceptance: Source author/work/edition monitoring flags are preserved as evidence and create no active acquisition before preview confirmation.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 imports confirmed eBook targets; B7 separately previews and imports audiobook targets.

rows.acceptance: Bulk author monitoring offers specific, future, or all-work policies with a count preview and separate confirmation.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 stores source flags but does not enable blanket author automation.

rows.acceptance: Open Library remains primary, Google Books is optional enrichment, and Hardcover is added as the required secondary adapter because Open Library resolves only 31 of 40 corpus cases.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 stores source Bookshelf/Hardcover IDs with provenance and never equates cross-provider IDs without evidence.

rows.acceptance: Ambiguous metadata or edition evidence produces an explained unresolved/held outcome instead of first-result selection.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 preview lists every unresolved source item and performs no download or file move for it.

rows.acceptance: Existing request approval, authorization, quota, audit, and notification primitives are reused for book requests.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 creates no historical requester identity where Bookshelf has none.

rows.acceptance: No Calibre adapter is required while the observed deployment publishes directly to Booklore and Audiobookshelf roots.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 never writes a Calibre database or invokes calibredb for this cutover.

rows.acceptance: The first release never performs automatic quality upgrades or format conversion.
rows.migration_consequence: B6 adopts current accepted files as-is and preserves explicit replacement as the only upgrade path.
